newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mosenergo gets SEC exemption for ADR.
newsitem.headline: Mosenergo gets SEC exemption for ADR.

text.p: Russia's power utility AO Mosenergo received an exemption on reporting requirements from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for the company's forthcoming American Depositary Receipts issue, a company official said on Friday.
"We are now preparing a depositary agreement with Bank of New York," securities department head Natalya Khokholkova told Reuters. "As soon as it is ready, we shall issue Level One ADRs immediately."
Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom is preparing documents for the agreement, she said, adding the preparation could take a month or a month and a half.
Currently Mosenergo ADRs issued in a private placement are traded on Western markets. The ADR closed at 44.50 marks in Berlin.
Level One ADRs give Western investors access to Mosenergo shares, but the company receives no revenues from the operations.
Mosenergo said on Friday its net profit in 1995 rose to $383 million from $129 million in 1994 according to U.S. GAAP. Its sales were $2.93 billion after $1.93 billion in 1994.
Khokholkova said the board would approve the company's plans for 1997 in January and a financial report on the 1996 results would be ready by February 25, 1997.
At 1730 GMT Mosenergo was traded at $0.994 after $0.999 at Thursday's close.
